raw: CHAPTER II. A Sight
en: [Chapter 2] A Sight

raw: “You know the Old Bailey well, no doubt?” said one of the oldest of clerks to Jerry the messenger.
en: "You know the Old Bailey courthouse well, no doubt?" said one of the oldest clerks to Jerry the messenger.
ko: "올드 베일리 법원이라면 잘 알고 있겠지?" 가장 나이 많은 서기 중 한 명이 메신저인 제리에게 말했다.

raw: “Ye-es, sir,” returned Jerry, in something of a dogged manner. “I _do_ know the Bailey.”
en: "Yes, sir," returned Jerry in a stubborn voice. "I _do_ know the Bailey."
ko: "네, 선생님," 제리가 고집스러운 목소리로 대답했다. "베일리에 대해선 _잘_ 알고 있습니다."

raw: “Just so.
en: "Just so.
ko: "그렇군.

raw: And you know Mr.
en: And you know Mr.
ko: 그리고 미스터

raw: Lorry.”
en: Lorry."
ko: 로리도 알겠지."

raw: “I know Mr.
en: "I know Mr.
ko: "미스터

raw: Lorry, sir, much better than I know the Bailey.
en: Lorry, sir, much better than I know the Bailey." He said it the way a reluctant witness answers in court.
ko: 로리라면 법원보다 훨씬 잘 알고 있습니다, 선생님." 그는 마치 법정에서 마지못해 증언하는 증인처럼 말했다.

raw: Much better,” said Jerry, not unlike a reluctant witness at the establishment in question, “than I, as a honest tradesman, wish to know the Bailey.”
en: "Much better than I, as an honest tradesman, wish to know the Bailey."
ko: "정직한 상인인 제가 법원을 아는 것보다야 훨씬 잘 알죠."

raw: “Very well.
en: "Very well.
ko: "아주 좋네.

raw: Find the door where the witnesses go in, and show the door-keeper this note for Mr.
en: Find the door where the witnesses go in, and show the doorkeeper this note for Mr.
ko: 증인들이 들어가는 문을 찾아가서, 문지기에게 미스터

raw: Lorry.
en: Lorry.
ko: 로리에게 전할 이 쪽지를 보여주게.

raw: He will then let you in.”
en: He will then let you in."
ko: 그러면 그가 안으로 들여보내 줄 걸세."

raw: “Into the court, sir?”
en: "Into the courtroom, sir?"
ko: "법정 안으로 말입니까, 선생님?"

raw: “Into the court.”
en: "Into the courtroom."
ko: "법정 안으로."

raw: Mr.
en: Mr.
ko: 미스터

raw: Cruncher’s eyes seemed to get a little closer to one another, and to interchange the inquiry, “What do you think of this?”
en: Cruncher’s eyes seemed to get a little closer together, as if asking each other, "What do you think of this?"
ko: 크런처의 양 눈이 약간 더 가까워진 것 같았는데, 마치 서로 \"이게 어떻게 된 일일까?\" 하고 묻는 듯했다.

raw: “Am I to wait in the court, sir?” he asked, as the result of that conference.
en: "Am I to wait in the court, sir?" he asked, after considering the idea.
ko: "법정 안에서 기다려야 합니까, 선생님?" 그는 그 생각에 잠시 잠겨 있다가 물었다.

raw: “I am going to tell you.
en: "I am going to tell you.
ko: "이제 말해주지.

raw: The door-keeper will pass the note to Mr.
en: The doorkeeper will pass the note to Mr.
ko: 문지기가 쪽지를 미스터

raw: Lorry, and do you make any gesture that will attract Mr.
en: Lorry. You must make some gesture to attract Mr.
ko: 로리에게 전할 거야. 자네는 미스터

raw: Lorry’s attention, and show him where you stand.
en: Lorry’s attention and show him where you are standing.
ko: 로리의 주의를 끌 몸짓을 해서, 자네가 어디에 서 있는지 알려줘야 하네.

raw: Then what you have to do, is, to remain there until he wants you.”
en: Then, your job is simply to stay there until he needs you."
ko: 그다음엔 그가 자네를 부를 때까지 그냥 거기 머물러 있으면 돼."

raw: “Is that all, sir?”
en: "Is that all, sir?"
ko: "그게 전부입니까, 선생님?"

raw: “That’s all.
en: "That’s all.
ko: "그게 전부야.

raw: He wishes to have a messenger at hand.
en: He wants to have a messenger nearby.
ko: 그는 메신저를 가까운 곳에 두고 싶어 하거든.

raw: This is to tell him you are there.”
en: This note is just to let him know you have arrived."
ko: 이 쪽지는 그저 자네가 도착했다는 걸 알리기 위한 것뿐이네."

raw: As the ancient clerk deliberately folded and superscribed the note, Mr.
en: As the old clerk slowly folded and addressed the note, Mr.
ko: 나이 든 서기가 천천히 쪽지를 접고 주소를 적는 동안, 미스터

raw: Cruncher, after surveying him in silence until he came to the blotting-paper stage, remarked:
en: Cruncher watched him in silence until he began using the blotting paper to dry the ink. Then Jerry remarked:
ko: 크런처는 그가 압지를 사용하여 잉크를 말리기 시작할 때까지 말없이 그를 지켜보았다. 그러고 나서 제리가 말했다:

raw: “I suppose they’ll be trying Forgeries this morning?”
en: "I suppose they’ll be trying forgery cases this morning?"
ko: "오늘 아침엔 위조 사건을 재판하나 보죠?"

raw: “Treason!”
en: "Treason!"
ko: "반역죄야!"

raw: “That’s quartering,” said Jerry. “Barbarous!”
en: "That means drawing and quartering," said Jerry. "Barbarous!"
ko: "사지를 찢고 토막 내겠군요," 제리가 말했다. "야만적이네요!"

raw: “It is the law,” remarked the ancient clerk, turning his surprised spectacles upon him. “It is the law.”
en: "It is the law," remarked the old clerk, turning his spectacles toward him in surprise. "It is the law."
ko: "그게 법이라네," 나이 든 서기가 놀라 안경 너머로 그를 보며 말했다. "법이 그렇다네."

raw: “It’s hard in the law to spile a man, I think.
en: "I think it’s harsh for the law to ruin a man's body like that.
ko: "법이 사람의 몸을 그렇게 망가뜨리는 건 가혹하다고 생각합니다.

raw: It’s hard enough to kill him, but it’s wery hard to spile him, sir.”
en: It’s hard enough to kill him, but it’s very hard to slice him up, sir."
ko: 죽이는 것만으로도 힘든데, 사람을 토막 내는 건 정말 끔찍한 일이죠, 선생님."

raw: “Not at all,” retained the ancient clerk. “Speak well of the law.
en: "Not at all," replied the old clerk. "Speak well of the law.
ko: "전혀 그렇지 않아," 나이 든 서기가 대답했다. "법에 대해선 좋게 말하게.

raw: Take care of your chest and voice, my good friend, and leave the law to take care of itself.
en: Take care of your own health, my friend, and leave the law to take care of itself.
ko: 자네 건강이나 잘 챙기게나, 친구. 법은 법이 알아서 하게 두고.

raw: I give you that advice.”
en: That is my advice to you."
ko: 이게 자네에게 주는 내 충고라네."

raw: “It’s the damp, sir, what settles on my chest and voice,” said Jerry. “I leave you to judge what a damp way of earning a living mine is.”
en: "It’s the damp weather, sir, that settles in my chest and voice," said Jerry. "You can imagine what a damp way of earning a living mine is."
ko: "선생님, 제 가슴과 목소리를 가라앉게 하는 건 바로 축축한 날씨 때문입니다," 제리가 말했다. "제가 밥벌이하는 방식이 얼마나 눅눅한지 상상이 가실 겁니다."

raw: “Well, well,” said the old clerk; “we all have our various ways of gaining a livelihood.
en: "Well, well," said the old clerk. "We all have our different ways of making a living.
ko: "글쎄, 글쎄," 나이 든 서기가 말했다. "우린 모두 각자 다른 방식으로 먹고사는 법이지.

raw: Some of us have damp ways, and some of us have dry ways.
en: Some of us have damp ways, and some have dry ways.
ko: 어떤 사람들은 눅눅한 방식을 쓰고, 어떤 사람들은 건조한 방식을 쓰니까.

raw: Here is the letter.
en: Here is the letter.
ko: 여기 편지가 있네.

raw: Go along.”
en: Off you go."
ko: 이제 가보게."

raw: Jerry took the letter, and, remarking to himself with less internal deference than he made an outward show of, “You are a lean old one, too,” made his bow, informed his son, in passing, of his destination, and went his way.
en: Jerry took the letter. Under his breath, with far less respect than his polite bow suggested, he muttered, "You are a withered old man yourself." He told his son where he was going as he walked past him. Then he went on his way.
ko: 제리는 편지를 받았다. 그는 공손하게 숙인 고개와는 사뭇 다르게, 존경심을 쏙 뺀 목소리로 "영감님 본인도 쪼그라든 늙은이면서"라고 작게 중얼거렸다. 그는 아들 곁을 지나가며 어디로 가는지 말해주었다. 그러고는 제 갈 길을 갔다.

raw: They hanged at Tyburn, in those days, so the street outside Newgate had not obtained one infamous notoriety that has since attached to it.
en: In those days, executions were carried out at Tyburn, so the street outside Newgate Prison had not yet gained the infamous reputation it would have later.
ko: 그 시절에는 사형 집행이 타이번에서 이루어졌기 때문에, 뉴게이트 감옥 밖의 거리는 훗날 얻게 될 악명을 아직 얻지 못한 상태였다.

raw: But, the gaol was a vile place, in which most kinds of debauchery and villainy were practised, and where dire diseases were bred, that came into court with the prisoners, and sometimes rushed straight from the dock at my Lord Chief Justice himself, and pulled him off the bench.
en: However, the prison itself was a filthy, corrupt place where all kinds of vice and crime were practiced and where terrible diseases bred. These illnesses often came into the courtroom with the prisoners, sometimes spreading directly to the Lord Chief Justice himself and killing him.
ko: 하지만 감옥 자체는 온갖 악덕과 범죄가 판을 치고 끔찍한 질병이 번식하는, 불결하고 부패한 장소였다. 이러한 질병은 종종 죄수들과 함께 법정에 들어와, 때로는 대법원장에게까지 직접 번져 그의 목숨을 앗아가기도 했다.

raw: It had more than once happened, that the Judge in the black cap pronounced his own doom as certainly as the prisoner’s, and even died before him.
en: More than once, a judge wearing the black execution cap had pronounced his own death sentence along with the prisoner's, dying even before the condemned man did.
ko: 사형 선고용 검은 모자를 쓴 판사가 죄수와 함께 자신의 사형 선고를 내리게 되어, 정작 사형수보다 먼저 사망하는 일도 한두 번이 아니었다.

raw: For the rest, the Old Bailey was famous as a kind of deadly inn-yard, from which pale travellers set out continually, in carts and coaches, on a violent passage into the other world: traversing some two miles and a half of public street and road, and shaming few good citizens, if any.
en: Otherwise, the Old Bailey was famous as a deadly departure point. Pale travelers set out from there in carts and carriages, making a violent journey into the next world. They traveled two and a half miles through public streets. Any good citizens who watched had reason to feel ashamed.
ko: 그 외에도 올드 베일리는 죽음의 출발지로 악명이 높았다. 창백한 여행자들은 그곳에서 수레와 마차를 타고 저승을 향한 폭력적인 여정에 올랐다. 그들은 사람 많은 거리를 2.5마일이나 지나갔다. 지켜보는 선량한 시민이라면 누구라도 수치심을 느낄 만했다.

raw: So powerful is use, and so desirable to be good use in the beginning.
en: Such is the power of custom, showing how important it is to establish good customs in the first place.
ko: 관습의 힘이란 그런 것이어서, 애초에 좋은 관습을 세우는 것이 얼마나 중요한지 보여준다.

raw: It was famous, too, for the pillory, a wise old institution, that inflicted a punishment of which no one could foresee the extent; also, for the whipping-post, another dear old institution, very humanising and softening to behold in action; also, for extensive transactions in blood-money, another fragment of ancestral wisdom, systematically leading to the most frightful mercenary crimes that could be committed under Heaven.
en: The court was also famous for the pillory. It was a punishment where no one could predict how much harm the crowd might do. Then there was the whipping post ,  another beloved tradition. And there was the practice of paying reward money for catching criminals. That system reliably led to terrible crimes committed purely for greed.
ko: 이 법원은 또한 칼 씌우기 형벌로도 유명했다. 이는 군중이 얼마나 많은 해를 끼칠지 아무도 예측할 수 없는 형벌이었다. 그리고 많은 이들의 사랑을 받는 또 다른 전통인 태형 기둥도 있었다. 또한 범죄자를 잡으면 포상금을 주는 관행도 있었다. 그 제도는 확실하게 오직 탐욕만을 위해 저질러지는 끔찍한 범죄로 이어졌다.

raw: Altogether, the Old Bailey, at that date, was a choice illustration of the precept, that “Whatever is is right;” an aphorism that would be as final as it is lazy, did it not include the troublesome consequence, that nothing that ever was, was wrong.
en: Overall, the Old Bailey at that time was a prime example of the lazy saying, "Whatever is, is right." It's a tidy idea. It would be simple and final ,  except that it also means nothing in the past had ever been wrong.
ko: 전반적으로 당시의 올드 베일리는 "존재하는 모든 것은 옳다"라는 안일한 격언의 대표적인 사례였다. 깔끔한 생각이다. 그것은 과거에 그 무엇도 결코 잘못된 적이 없었다는 의미이기도 하다는 점만 제외하면, 단순하고도 단정적이었을 것이다.

raw: Making his way through the tainted crowd, dispersed up and down this hideous scene of action, with the skill of a man accustomed to make his way quietly, the messenger found out the door he sought, and handed in his letter through a trap in it.
en: Jerry moved through the dirty crowd with the quiet skill of a man who knew how to go unnoticed. He found the door he was looking for and passed his note through a small slot.
ko: 제리는 눈에 띄지 않게 다니는 법을 아는 자의 조용한 솜씨로 지저분한 군중 속을 헤치고 나아갔다. 그는 자기가 찾던 문을 발견하고는 작은 틈새로 쪽지를 밀어 넣었다.

raw: For, people then paid to see the play at the Old Bailey, just as they paid to see the play in Bedlam--only the former entertainment was much the dearer.
en: In those days, people paid to watch trials at the Old Bailey just as they paid to watch the patients at Bedlam asylum, except the trials cost much more.
ko: 그 시절 사람들은 베들럼 정신병원의 환자들을 구경하려고 돈을 냈던 것처럼, 올드 베일리에서 열리는 재판을 보기 위해 돈을 지불했다. 재판 구경 비용이 훨씬 비쌌다는 점만 다를 뿐이었다.

raw: Therefore, all the Old Bailey doors were well guarded--except, indeed, the social doors by which the criminals got there, and those were always left wide open.
en: Therefore, all the doors to the Old Bailey were heavily guarded, except for the doors the criminals entered through, which were always left wide open.
ko: 따라서 올드 베일리의 모든 문은 철저하게 경비되었는데, 범죄자들이 들어가는 문만 예외적으로 항상 활짝 열려 있었다.

raw: After some delay and demur, the door grudgingly turned on its hinges a very little way, and allowed Mr.
en: After some delay and discussion, the door opened slightly, allowing Mr.
ko: 약간의 지연과 실랑이 끝에, 문이 살짝 열려 미스터

raw: Jerry Cruncher to squeeze himself into court.
en: Jerry Cruncher to squeeze himself into the courtroom.
ko: 제리 크런처가 법정 안으로 비집고 들어갈 수 있었다.

raw: “What’s on?” he asked, in a whisper, of the man he found himself next to.
en: "What's happening?" he whispered to the man standing next to him.
ko: "무슨 일이죠?" 그가 옆에 서 있던 남자에게 속삭였다.

raw: “Nothing yet.”
en: "Nothing yet."
ko: "아직 아무 일도 없어."

raw: “What’s coming on?”
en: "What case is coming up?"
ko: "무슨 사건이 나올 차례인데요?"

raw: “The Treason case.”
en: "The treason case."
ko: "반역죄 사건."

raw: “The quartering one, eh?”
en: "The drawing and quartering one, right?"
ko: "사지를 찢고 토막 내는 거, 맞죠?"

raw: “Ah!” returned the man, with a relish; “he’ll be drawn on a hurdle to be half hanged, and then he’ll be taken down and sliced before his own face, and then his inside will be taken out and burnt while he looks on, and then his head will be chopped off, and he’ll be cut into quarters.
en: "Yes!" the man replied with excitement. "He’ll be dragged on a wooden frame to be half-hanged, then cut down and sliced up while he's still alive. His insides will be pulled out and burned before his eyes, then his head will be chopped off and his body cut into four pieces.
ko: "그렇지!" 그 남자가 흥분해서 대답했다. "그놈은 나무틀에 끌려가 반쯤 교수형을 당한 다음, 산 채로 내려져서 난도질당할 거야. 눈앞에서 내장을 꺼내 불태운 다음, 머리를 자르고 몸뚱이를 네 토막 내겠지.

raw: That’s the sentence.”
en: That’s the sentence."
ko: 형벌이 그렇단 말이야."

raw: “If he’s found Guilty, you mean to say?” Jerry added, by way of proviso.
en: "If he’s found guilty, you mean?" Jerry added, to clarify.
ko: "유죄 판결을 받으면 그렇다는 거죠?" 제리가 분명히 하려고 덧붙였다.

raw: “Oh! they’ll find him guilty,” said the other. “Don’t you be afraid of that.”
en: "Oh, they’ll find him guilty," said the other. "Don't you worry about that."
ko: "오, 그놈들은 그를 유죄로 만들 거야," 상대방이 말했다. "그건 걱정하지 마."

raw: Mr.
en: Mr.
ko: 미스터

raw: Cruncher’s attention was here diverted to the door-keeper, whom he saw making his way to Mr.
en: Cruncher’s attention was then drawn to the doorkeeper, whom he saw walking toward Mr.
ko: 크런처의 시선이 문지기에게 향했는데, 문지기가 미스터

raw: Lorry, with the note in his hand.
en: Lorry with the note.
ko: 로리를 향해 쪽지를 들고 걸어가는 것이 보였다.

raw: Mr.
en: Mr.
ko: 미스터

raw: Lorry sat at a table, among the gentlemen in wigs: not far from a wigged gentleman, the prisoner’s counsel, who had a great bundle of papers before him: and nearly opposite another wigged gentleman with his hands in his pockets, whose whole attention, when Mr.
en: Lorry sat at a table among the lawyers in wigs, not far from the prisoner’s defense lawyer, who had a large stack of papers in front of him. Nearly opposite sat another lawyer in a wig, with his hands in his pockets, who seemed entirely focused on staring at the courtroom ceiling.
ko: 로리는 가발을 쓴 변호사들 틈의 탁자에 앉아 있었는데, 앞에 서류 더미를 잔뜩 쌓아 둔 죄수 측 변호인과 멀지 않았다. 그 맞은편 부근에는 가발을 쓰고 주머니에 손을 찔러 넣은 다른 변호사가 앉아 있었는데, 그는 법정 천장을 뚫어져라 쳐다보는 데만 완전히 집중하고 있는 것 같았다.

raw: Cruncher looked at him then or afterwards, seemed to be concentrated on the ceiling of the court.
en: Whenever Mr. Cruncher looked at him, whether right then or later on, the man seemed to be completely focused on the courtroom ceiling.
ko: 그때든 나중이든, 미스터 크런처가 그를 볼 때마다, 그 남자는 법정 천장에만 온통 집중하고 있는 듯했다.

raw: After some gruff coughing and rubbing of his chin and signing with his hand, Jerry attracted the notice of Mr.
en: It took some effort, but he finally caught Mr. Lorry's eye. Mr.
ko: 애를 좀 쓴 끝에, 그는 마침내 미스터 로리와 눈이 마주쳤다. 미스터

raw: Lorry, who had stood up to look for him, and who quietly nodded and sat down again.
en: Lorry had stood up to look for him. He nodded quietly and sat back down.
ko: 로리는 그를 찾으려고 자리에서 일어난 터였다. 그는 조용히 고개를 끄덕이곤 다시 자리에 앉았다.

raw: “What’s _he_ got to do with the case?” asked the man he had spoken with.
en: "What does _he_ have to do with the case?" asked the man Jerry had been talking to.
ko: "_저 사람_이 이 사건이랑 무슨 상관이지?" 제리와 이야기하던 남자가 물었다.

raw: “Blest if I know,” said Jerry.
en: "I have no idea," said Jerry.
ko: "나도 모릅니다," 제리가 말했다.

raw: “What have _you_ got to do with it, then, if a person may inquire?”
en: "What do _you_ have to do with it, then, if I may ask?"
ko: "그럼 물어보겠는데, _당신_은 이 일과 무슨 상관이오?"

raw: “Blest if I know that either,” said Jerry.
en: "I don't know that either," said Jerry.
ko: "그것도 모르겠습니다," 제리가 말했다.

raw: The entrance of the Judge, and a consequent great stir and settling down in the court, stopped the dialogue.
en: The entrance of the Judge and the general movement of the crowd settling into their places stopped their conversation.
ko: 판사의 입장과 함께 사람들이 제자리를 찾아가는 어수선한 움직임 때문에 그들의 대화는 멈췄다.

raw: Presently, the dock became the central point of interest.
en: Soon, the prisoner's dock became the center of attention.
ko: 이내 피고인석이 시선의 중심이 되었다.

raw: Two gaolers, who had been standing there, went out, and the prisoner was brought in, and put to the bar.
en: Two guards who had been standing there stepped out, and the prisoner was brought in and placed at the bar.
ko: 그곳에 서 있던 경비병 두 명이 밖으로 나오자, 죄수가 끌려 들어와 법대에 섰다.

raw: Everybody present, except the one wigged gentleman who looked at the ceiling, stared at him.
en: Everyone in the courtroom, except the lawyer looking at the ceiling, stared at him.
ko: 천장을 보고 있던 변호사를 제외하고 법정 안의 모든 사람이 그를 빤히 쳐다보았다.

raw: All the human breath in the place, rolled at him, like a sea, or a wind, or a fire.
en: The breath of the crowd seemed to rush toward him like a wave, a wind, or a fire.
ko: 군중의 숨결이 마치 파도나 바람, 혹은 불길처럼 그를 향해 밀어닥치는 듯했다.

raw: Eager faces strained round pillars and corners, to get a sight of him; spectators in back rows stood up, not to miss a hair of him; people on the floor of the court, laid their hands on the shoulders of the people before them, to help themselves, at anybody’s cost, to a view of him--stood a-tiptoe, got upon ledges, stood upon next to nothing, to see every inch of him.
en: Eager faces leaned around pillars and corners to see him. Spectators in the back rows stood up so they wouldn't miss a single detail. People on the floor put their hands on the shoulders of those in front of them to get a better view. They stood on tiptoe and climbed onto ledges.
ko: 열띤 얼굴들이 그를 보기 위해 기둥과 모서리 주위로 몸을 기울였다. 뒷줄의 방청객들은 단 하나도 놓치지 않으려고 자리에서 일어났다. 바닥에 있는 사람들은 더 잘 보려고 앞에 있는 사람들의 어깨에 손을 얹었다. 그들은 발돋움을 하고 난간 위로 기어 올라갔다.

raw: Conspicuous among these latter, like an animated bit of the spiked wall of Newgate, Jerry stood: aiming at the prisoner the beery breath of a whet he had taken as he came along, and discharging it to mingle with the waves of other beer, and gin, and tea, and coffee, and what not, that flowed at him, and already broke upon the great windows behind him in an impure mist and rain.
en: Standing out among them was Jerry. He looked like a piece of the spiked wall of Newgate Prison. He breathed out the smell of the beer he had drunk on the way. That smell joined the thick, damp air of the crowded room ,  the air that was slowly misting up the large windows behind the prisoner.
ko: 그들 사이에서 제리가 눈에 띄었다. 그는 뉴게이트 감옥의 못 박힌 벽 한 조각처럼 보였다. 그는 오면서 마신 맥주 냄새를 풍겼다. 그 냄새는 인파로 가득 찬 방의 짙고 축축한 공기, 즉 죄수 뒤편의 커다란 창문에 서서히 김을 서리게 하던 그 공기와 섞였다.

raw: The object of all this staring and blaring, was a young man of about five-and-twenty, well-grown and well-looking, with a sunburnt cheek and a dark eye.
en: The target of all this attention was a young man of about twenty-five, tall, well-built, with sunburnt skin and dark eyes.
ko: 이 모든 관심의 대상은 스물다섯 살쯤 되어 보이는 젊은이로, 키가 크고 체격이 좋으며 햇볕에 그을린 피부와 어두운 눈동자를 가졌다.

raw: His condition was that of a young gentleman.
en: He looked like a young gentleman.
ko: 그는 젊은 신사처럼 보였다.

raw: He was plainly dressed in black, or very dark grey, and his hair, which was long and dark, was gathered in a ribbon at the back of his neck; more to be out of his way than for ornament.
en: He was dressed plainly in black or dark gray, and his long, dark hair was tied back with a ribbon, more to keep it out of the way than for style.
ko: 그는 검은색이나 짙은 회색 옷을 수수하게 차려입었고, 그의 긴 검은 머리는 멋을 내기 위해서라기보다 거치적거리지 않게 하려고 리본으로 묶여 있었다.

raw: As an emotion of the mind will express itself through any covering of the body, so the paleness which his situation engendered came through the brown upon his cheek, showing the soul to be stronger than the sun.
en: Just as strong emotions show through any clothing, the paleness caused by his dangerous situation showed through his sunburned cheeks, proving that his inner feelings were stronger than the sun.
ko: 강렬한 감정은 어떤 옷을 입어도 겉으로 드러나는 법이듯, 그가 처한 위험한 상황이 자아낸 창백함이 햇볕에 그을린 뺨 사이로 비치며 내면의 감정이 태양보다 강하다는 것을 증명했다.

raw: He was otherwise quite self-possessed, bowed to the Judge, and stood quiet.
en: Otherwise, he was quite calm, bowed to the Judge, and stood quietly.
ko: 그 외에는 그는 꽤 차분했으며, 판사에게 인사를 하고 조용히 서 있었다.

raw: The sort of interest with which this man was stared and breathed at, was not a sort that elevated humanity.
en: The interest with which the crowd stared and breathed on this man was not a noble human feeling.
ko: 군중이 이 남자를 쳐다보며 숨을 내뿜게 한 그 관심은 결코 고상한 인간의 감정이 아니었다.

raw: Had he stood in peril of a less horrible sentence--had there been a chance of any one of its savage details being spared--by just so much would he have lost in his fascination.
en: If he had been facing a less terrible sentence, or if there had been any chance he would be spared its brutal details, he would have been far less fascinating to them.
ko: 그가 덜 끔찍한 형벌을 앞두고 있었거나, 그 잔인한 과정들을 면할 가능성이 조금이라도 있었다면, 그들에게 이처럼 큰 흥미를 끌지는 못했을 것이다.

raw: The form that was to be doomed to be so shamefully mangled, was the sight; the immortal creature that was to be so butchered and torn asunder, yielded the sensation.
en: The body that was doomed to be so horribly mutilated was the main attraction; the human being about to be butchered was the source of the excitement.
ko: 그렇게 끔찍하게 훼손될 운명에 처한 육체가 주된 볼거리였으며, 도살당하기 직전의 인간이 그 흥분의 근원이었다.

raw: Whatever gloss the various spectators put upon the interest, according to their several arts and powers of self-deceit, the interest was, at the root of it, Ogreish.
en: Whatever excuses the spectators made for their interest, at its root, it was a savage, monstrous curiosity.
ko: 방청객들이 자신들의 관심에 대해 어떤 변명을 하든 간에, 그 뿌리에는 야만적이고 기괴한 호기심이 있었다.

raw: Silence in the court!
en: "Silence in court!" was called.
ko: "법숙 정숙!" 하는 외침이 울렸다.

raw: Charles Darnay had yesterday pleaded Not Guilty to an indictment denouncing him (with infinite jingle and jangle) for that he was a false traitor to our serene, illustrious, excellent, and so forth, prince, our Lord the King, by reason of his having, on divers occasions, and by divers means and ways, assisted Lewis, the French King, in his wars against our said serene, illustrious, excellent, and so forth; that was to say, by coming and going, between the dominions of our said serene, illustrious, excellent, and so forth, and those of the said French Lewis, and wickedly, falsely, traitorously, and otherwise evil-adverbiously, revealing to the said French Lewis what forces our said serene, illustrious, excellent, and so forth, had in preparation to send to Canada and North America.
en: Charles Darnay had pleaded not guilty the day before to a long, repetitive indictment charging him with being a traitor to our king. He was accused of having assisted Louis, the King of France, in his wars against England on several occasions. The charges claimed he did this by traveling back and forth between England and France, revealing to the French king what military forces England was preparing to send to Canada and North America.
ko: 찰스 다네이는 우리 국왕에 대한 반역자라는 길고 반복적인 기소장에 대해 전날 무죄를 주장한 바 있었다. 그는 프랑스의 루이 국왕이 영국을 상대로 벌인 전쟁을 여러 차례 도왔다는 혐의를 받고 있었다. 기소장에는 그가 영국과 프랑스를 오가며 영국이 캐나다와 북미로 보낼 군사력을 프랑스 국왕에게 누설하는 방식으로 그런 짓을 했다고 적혀 있었다.

raw: This much, Jerry, with his head becoming more and more spiky as the law terms bristled it, made out with huge satisfaction, and so arrived circuitously at the understanding that the aforesaid, and over and over again aforesaid, Charles Darnay, stood there before him upon his trial; that the jury were swearing in; and that Mr.
en: Jerry's hair seemed to stand up even more as the complicated legal terms were read. He listened with satisfaction. He figured out that this Charles Darnay was indeed the man on trial. The jury was being sworn in.
ko: 복잡한 법률 용어들이 낭독되자 제리의 머리카락이 한층 더 곤두서는 것 같았다. 그는 흡족하게 귀를 기울였다. 그는 이 찰스 다네이가 틀림없이 재판을 받고 있는 그 남자라는 것을 알아차렸다. 배심원들이 선서를 하고 있었다.

raw: Attorney-General was making ready to speak.
en: The Attorney General was preparing to speak.
ko: 검찰총장이 발언을 준비하고 있었다.

raw: The accused, who was (and who knew he was) being mentally hanged, beheaded, and quartered, by everybody there, neither flinched from the situation, nor assumed any theatrical air in it.
en: The accused man knew that everyone in the room was already imagining him hanged, beheaded, and quartered. He did not panic. He did not act dramatically.
ko: 피고인은 법정 안의 모든 사람이 이미 그가 교수형에 처해지고 참수당하고 사지가 찢기는 모습을 상상하고 있다는 것을 알고 있었습니다. 그는 당황하지 않았습니다. 그는 극적으로 행동하지도 않았습니다.

raw: He was quiet and attentive; watched the opening proceedings with a grave interest; and stood with his hands resting on the slab of wood before him, so composedly, that they had not displaced a leaf of the herbs with which it was strewn.
en: He was quiet and attentive, watching the start of the trial with serious interest. He stood with his hands resting on the wooden bar in front of him so calmly that he didn't even stir the herbs scattered on it.
ko: 그는 조용하고 주의 깊게, 진지한 관심을 가지고 재판이 시작되는 것을 지켜보았습니다. 그는 자신 앞에 있는 나무 난간에 손을 얹고 너무나 차분하게 서 있어서 그 위에 흩어진 허브조차 흔들리지 않았습니다.

raw: The court was all bestrewn with herbs and sprinkled with vinegar, as a precaution against gaol air and gaol fever.
en: The courtroom was covered in herbs and sprinkled with vinegar to protect against the bad air and prison fever.
ko: 법정은 나쁜 공기와 감옥 열병을 막기 위해 허브로 덮여 있었고 식초가 뿌려져 있었습니다.

raw: Over the prisoner’s head there was a mirror, to throw the light down upon him.
en: Over the prisoner’s head hung a mirror to reflect light down on him.
ko: 죄수의 머리 위에는 그에게 빛을 반사하기 위한 거울이 걸려 있었습니다.

raw: Crowds of the wicked and the wretched had been reflected in it, and had passed from its surface and this earth’s together.
en: Over the years, crowds of desperate and criminal people had been reflected in it before leaving both the courtroom and the earth.
ko: 수년 동안, 절망에 빠진 범죄자 무리가 법정과 이 세상을 떠나기 전에 그 거울에 비춰졌습니다.

raw: Haunted in a most ghastly manner that abominable place would have been, if the glass could ever have rendered back its reflections, as the ocean is one day to give up its dead.
en: That terrible place would have been haunted indeed if the glass could show all the faces it had once reflected, just as the ocean will one day give up its dead.
ko: 언젠가 바다가 죽은 자들을 내어주듯, 그 거울이 한때 비추었던 모든 얼굴을 보여줄 수 있다면 그 끔찍한 장소는 참으로 유령이 출몰하는 곳이었을 것입니다.

raw: Some passing thought of the infamy and disgrace for which it had been reserved, may have struck the prisoner’s mind.
en: Perhaps some thought of the disgrace associated with that mirror crossed the prisoner’s mind.
ko: 어쩌면 그 거울과 관련된 불명예에 대한 어떤 생각이 죄수의 마음을 스쳤을지도 모릅니다.

raw: Be that as it may, a change in his position making him conscious of a bar of light across his face, he looked up; and when he saw the glass his face flushed, and his right hand pushed the herbs away.
en: In any case, as he shifted his position and felt a beam of light hit his face, he looked up. When he saw the mirror, his face flushed, and his right hand pushed the herbs aside.
ko: 어쨌든, 그가 자세를 바꾸고 한 줄기 빛이 자신의 얼굴에 닿는 것을 느꼈을 때, 그는 위를 쳐다보았습니다. 거울을 보았을 때, 그의 얼굴은 붉어졌고 오른손으로 허브를 밀어냈습니다.

raw: It happened, that the action turned his face to that side of the court which was on his left.
en: This movement caused him to turn his face to the left side of the court.
ko: 이 움직임으로 인해 그는 법정의 왼쪽으로 얼굴을 돌리게 되었습니다.

raw: About on a level with his eyes, there sat, in that corner of the Judge’s bench, two persons upon whom his look immediately rested; so immediately, and so much to the changing of his aspect, that all the eyes that were turned upon him, turned to them.
en: On a level with his eyes, sitting in the corner of the Judge’s bench, were two people who caught his attention immediately. His expression changed so suddenly when he saw them that all eyes in the room followed his gaze.
ko: 그의 눈높이에, 판사석 구석에 앉아 있는 두 사람이 즉시 그의 시선을 끌었습니다. 그들을 보았을 때 그의 표정이 너무나 갑작스럽게 변했기 때문에 방 안의 모든 시선이 그의 시선을 따라갔습니다.

raw: The spectators saw in the two figures, a young lady of little more than twenty, and a gentleman who was evidently her father; a man of a very remarkable appearance in respect of the absolute whiteness of his hair, and a certain indescribable intensity of face: not of an active kind, but pondering and self-communing.
en: The spectators saw a young lady of just over twenty and a gentleman who was clearly her father. He was a man of very striking appearance, with pure white hair and an intense, thoughtful face.
ko: 관중들은 스무 살이 조금 넘은 젊은 숙녀와 그녀의 아버지임이 분명한 한 신사를 보았습니다. 그는 순백의 머리카락과 강렬하고 사색적인 얼굴을 가진, 매우 인상적인 외모의 남자였습니다.

raw: When this expression was upon him, he looked as if he were old; but when it was stirred and broken up--as it was now, in a moment, on his speaking to his daughter--he became a handsome man, not past the prime of life.
en: When he was lost in thought, he looked quite old; but when he was engaged, as he was now, speaking to his daughter, he became a handsome man who seemed to still be in his prime.
ko: 생각에 잠겨 있을 때 그는 꽤 늙어 보였지만, 지금처럼 딸에게 말을 걸며 몰두하고 있을 때는 여전히 전성기에 있는 듯한 잘생긴 남자가 되었습니다.

raw: His daughter had one of her hands drawn through his arm, as she sat by him, and the other pressed upon it.
en: His daughter sat beside him with one hand resting on his arm and the other pressing against it.
ko: 그의 딸은 한 손은 그의 팔에 얹고 다른 한 손은 그 팔을 꽉 누른 채 그의 곁에 앉아 있었습니다.

raw: She had drawn close to him, in her dread of the scene, and in her pity for the prisoner.
en: She had drawn close to him in her fear of the courtroom and her pity for the prisoner.
ko: 그녀는 법정에 대한 두려움과 죄수에 대한 연민 때문에 그에게 바짝 다가가 있었습니다.

raw: Her forehead had been strikingly expressive of an engrossing terror and compassion that saw nothing but the peril of the accused.
en: Her face showed deep terror and compassion, focused entirely on the danger facing the accused man.
ko: 그녀의 얼굴은 깊은 공포와 연민을 보여주었으며, 기소된 남자가 직면한 위험에 온전히 집중하고 있었습니다.

raw: This had been so very noticeable, so very powerfully and naturally shown, that starers who had had no pity for him were touched by her; and the whisper went about, “Who are they?”
en: This was so clear and natural that even the spectators who felt no pity for him were touched by her expression, and a whisper went around: "Who are they?"
ko: 이것은 너무나 명확하고 자연스러워서 죄수에게 연민을 느끼지 않던 관중들조차 그녀의 표정에 감동받았고, 속삭임이 퍼졌습니다. 그들은 누구인가?

raw: Jerry, the messenger, who had made his own observations, in his own manner, and who had been sucking the rust off his fingers in his absorption, stretched his neck to hear who they were.
en: Jerry the messenger, who had been watching in his own way and sucking the rust off his fingers, stretched his neck to hear the answer.
ko: 자기만의 방식으로 지켜보며 손가락의 녹을 빨아먹고 있던 메신저 제리는 대답을 듣기 위해 목을 길게 뺐습니다.

raw: The crowd about him had pressed and passed the inquiry on to the nearest attendant, and from him it had been more slowly pressed and passed back; at last it got to Jerry:
en: The question was passed through the crowd to the nearest court official and then whispered back until it reached Jerry:
ko: 질문은 군중을 지나 가장 가까운 법원 관리에게 전달되었고, 그런 다음 다시 제리에게 도달할 때까지 속삭임으로 돌아왔습니다.

raw: “Witnesses.”
en: "Witnesses."
ko: 증인들.

raw: “For which side?”
en: "For which side?"
ko: 어느 쪽의?

raw: “Against.”
en: "Against."
ko: 반대편.

raw: “Against what side?”
en: "Against who?"
ko: 누구를 반대하여?

raw: “The prisoner’s.”
en: "Against the prisoner."
ko: 죄수를 반대하여.

raw: The Judge, whose eyes had gone in the general direction, recalled them, leaned back in his seat, and looked steadily at the man whose life was in his hand, as Mr.
en: The Judge's eyes had followed the crowd's gaze. Now he looked back. He leaned back in his seat and stared steadily at the man whose life was in his hands.
ko: 판사의 눈은 군중의 시선을 쫓고 있었습니다. 이제 그는 다시 뒤돌아보았습니다. 그는 자리에 기대어 앉아 목숨이 자신의 손에 달려 있는 그 남자를 빤히 쳐다보았습니다.

raw: Attorney-General rose to spin the rope, grind the axe, and hammer the nails into the scaffold.
en: The Attorney General rose to begin building the case for his execution.
ko: 법무장관이 그를 사형에 처하기 위한 논고를 시작하려고 일어섰습니다.
